title: Biased discrete derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, $p\in\mathbb R$, $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. For each $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, define the biased discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ by $D_i^{(p)}f(x)=\beta_p\bigl(f(x^{i\to 1})-f(x^{i\to -1})\bigr)/2$, where $x^{i\to a}$ is obtained by setting coordinate $i$ of $x$ to $a$ and $\beta_p$ denotes the bias normalization factor.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ is an index among the $n$ coordinates
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
caveat: The supplied statement uses a bias normalization factor but does not define its mathematical value.
